AUDIENCE & TESTABILITY:
API audience: INTERNAL-FRAMEWORK.
Harness testability: TESTABLE.
Scoring recommendation: include only in advanced/internal bucket.

ROOT CAUSE:
The snippet misread the behavior of the function by assuming it reduces extended chords all the way down to triads (e.g., `"maj9"` to `"maj"` and `{"7", "9"}`). The source code explicitly maps `"maj9"` to its 7th chord equivalent `"maj7"` and extracts only the upper extension `{"9"}`.

CORRECT USAGE:
```python
import mir_eval.chord

base_quality, extensions = mir_eval.chord.reduce_extended_quality("maj9")

assert base_quality == "maj7"
assert extensions == {"9"}
```

REQUIRED TYPES & IMPORTS:
`mir_eval.chord`

DOC MUST SAY:
- The function maps extended qualities to their 7th chord equivalents (e.g., `"maj9"` maps to `"maj7"` and `{"9"}`), not to triads.
- If the quality is not in the predefined reduction dictionary, it returns the original quality and an empty set.
